condition: Clostridioides difficile infection complicating a UC flare
permutationLabel: C. difficile positive, on azathioprine, recent antibiotics
summary: 52-year-old woman with UC on azathioprine, 8 loose bloody stools/day after ciprofloxacin for a UTI; C. difficile GDH and toxin positive. Treat CDI (oral vancomycin or fidaxomicin); do not escalate immunosuppression on the assumption of a simple flare.

inputs.hpi: Ulcerative colitis on azathioprine and mesalazine, in remission for 2 years. Took ciprofloxacin for a urinary infection 10 days ago. Now 8 loose stools a day with some blood, crampy pain, feels hot. Stool test sent by GP: C. difficile GDH positive, toxin positive.

exam.abdomen: Soft, mild diffuse tenderness, not distended, no peritonism.

labs.name: C. difficile GDH / toxin
labs.resultText: GDH positive; toxin A/B EIA positive

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Clostridioides difficile infection with ulcerative colitis flare
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: C. difficile infection (toxin positive) in a patient with ulcerative colitis on azathioprine, after ciprofloxacin. Treat CDI; reassess colitis activity.

mustInclude.note: IDSA/SHEA 2021: fidaxomicin (preferred) or oral vancomycin for an initial episode. ECCO 2021: treat CDI in IBD with vancomycin or fidaxomicin.
mustInclude.proposedFix: Add a C. difficile disease/protocol (triggers: recent antibiotics, hospital/care-home exposure, toxin-positive result): oral vancomycin or fidaxomicin; fulminant: oral/rectal vancomycin + IV metronidazole, surgical consultation (IDSA/SHEA 2017/2021, WSES 2019). Read a toxin-positive lab result.

guideline.name: ECCO guidelines — prevention, diagnosis and management of infections in IBD
guideline.section: Test for C. difficile in every flare; treat with vancomycin or fidaxomicin; immunosuppression decisions individualised
guideline.citation: Kucharzik T, Ellul P, Greuter T, et al. ECCO guidelines on the prevention, diagnosis, and management of infections in inflammatory bowel disease. J Crohns Colitis. 2021;15:879–913.

guideline.name: IDSA/SHEA focused update — management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults
guideline.section: Initial CDI episode: fidaxomicin preferred, oral vancomycin acceptable
guideline.citation: Johnson S, Lavergne V, Skinner AM, et al. Clinical practice guideline by the Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) and Society for Healthcare Epidemiology of America (SHEA): 2021 focused update guidelines on management of Clostridioides difficile infection in adults. Clin Infect Dis. 2021;73:e1029–e1044.

rationale: Permutation: an infective trigger with a positive toxin test and immunosuppression. The result is in the labs; the confirmed diagnosis is CDI (A04.7). Tests whether the plan treats the infection rather than the colitis alone.
